chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Amr al-Zayyat, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Whoever dies in Al-Medina, Allah will resurrect him among the Secured ones on the Day of Judgement – among them are Yahya ibn Habeeb, and Abu Ubeyda al-Haza’a, and Abdul Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj.

key_terms.أَبُو عُبَيْدَةَ الْحَذَّاءُ: Abu Ubeyda al-Haza’a (one of the named individuals)
key_terms.الْآمِنِينَ: The Secured / The Safe (a title for those protected from fear on Judgment Day)
key_terms.الْمَدِينَةِ: Al-Medina (the city, often referring to Medina al-Munawwarah)
key_terms.عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ الْحَجَّاجِ: Abdul Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj (one of the named individuals)
key_terms.يَحْيَى بْنُ حَبِيبٍ: Yahya ibn Habeeb (one of the named individuals)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for dying in Al-Medina according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* underscores the unique spiritual status of Medina, linking physical proximity to the Prophet’s city with divine security (*aman*) on the Day of Resurrection. By citing specific companions like Yahya ibn Habeeb, the narration emphasizes that this merit is not merely geographical but is realized through faithful adherence to the Ahl al-Bayt's teachings, reinforcing the concept of *Wilayah* as a source of salvation.
